sector_model: alternative asset manager: fee related earnings, distributable earnings, performance revenue and dividend; consolidated GAAP cash flow and debt not comparable
thesis: Blackstone Inc. (NYSE: BX), largest alternative asset manager. Q3 2026 (release Exhibit 99.1, 2026-10-22): GAAP net income to Blackstone 662M (+6%), Distributable Earnings 1.7B (-9%), DE per share 1.32 (vs 1.52, -13%), Fee Related Earnings 1.6B (+6%; 1.26 per share), fee-related performance revenues 540M (+19%), total AUM 1,368.3B (+10%), inflows 63.3B, deployment 30.1B, realizations 33.1B, net accrued performance revenues 7.3B (5.84 per share, -3% q/q). Dividend 1.12 for Q3, 5.06 over the last twelve months. At 120.17 (2026-11-13 close; 52-week 101.73-165.14, so about 27% below the high) TTM GAAP EPS is 4.49 (3.87 FY2025 + 3.19 9M26 - 2.57 9M25), P/E 26.8x; trailing dividend yield about 4.2% on 5.06. Q3 DE per share annualized would imply about 22.8x, shown only as context because realizations are lumpy. The market may be discounting weaker realizations and the 9% DE decline while fee earnings and AUM keep growing.
counterthesis: DE fell 9% and DE per share 13% while FRE rose 6%: earnings quality depends on performance revenues and realizations that are cyclical, and net accrued performance revenue slipped 3% q/q. Stock-based compensation was 1.25B in 9M26 and is a real cost; GAAP share count (751M Class A versus about 1.24B including partnership units) must be handled with care. Debt on the consolidated balance sheet is 13.4B including consolidated funds and a new 1.1B senior note offering (5.650% 2031 and 5.900% 2033, 8-K 2026-11-02, use of proceeds not stated). Private credit and real estate marks, retail product redemptions, fee compression and a weak realization market are thesis breakers. The stock is a large index holding, so it duplicates exposure already held in broad US funds.
invalidation: Thesis breaks if quarterly DE per share keeps falling with falling inflows, retail fund redemptions accelerate, net accrued performance revenue declines for several quarters, or fee-related earnings growth stalls.
